title: Rolling-20 active-engine Top20 hit-count regime
hypothesis: A rolling 20-target mean of the active engine's prior Top20 hit counts may contain more stable regime information than a single lagged hit count and may improve the next-target hit-count distribution.
target: H_t = |frozen Top20_{t-1} intersect draw_t|, taking values 0..5.

models.name: M1 lag-1 transition
models.state: a = previous target's observed Top20 hit count

models.name: M20 rolling-20 regime
models.state_definition: S_t = sum of the previous 20 observed Top20 hit counts, using only targets before t

evaluation.target_rows: source row index i=20..3202 inclusive; rolling state requires 20 prior observed outcomes
evaluation.update_order: Score target i before adding its outcome to either M1 or M20 counts. Every training row j must satisfy j<i; every rolling state uses only y[j-20..j-1].
evaluation.gain_definition: baseline loss minus model loss; positive means the model improves

inference.multiple_testing: Holm across all four predeclared comparison-endpoint p-values

guardrails: No parameter or bucket-boundary tuning after computation begins.
Discovery, validation and historical blind OOS are chronological; historical blind OOS is not a virgin holdout because related SONAR research has examined the same archive.
The rolling state predicts Top20 hit-count calibration only, not winning numbers.
The experiment family-wide multiplicity across Q00-Q115 is not corrected by the within-Q115 Holm procedure; all findings remain exploratory.
One prospective target is descriptive only and cannot justify promotion.
No changes to the active engine, Q60 freezes, or PRs #6, #7, #8.
next_action: Execute the fixed walk-forward once; persist the full target ledger, report, validation, deterministic runner and an immutable 2026-11-11 prospective distribution freeze. Await the official draw before scoring that freeze.
